brief: BofA expects Sep payrolls to rise a below-consensus 60k (private 50k), but frames this as seasonal payback from August's unusually favorable adjustment rather than genuine weakening: claims and ADP point to underlying growth near 100k+. The u-rate should hold 4.1% (LFPR steady at 61.6%), with upside risk to 4.2% from payback in August's household-survey surge. TPS visa revocations are a modest, gradual headwind. BofA argues the report won't move October hike odds because September CPI matters more to the Fed. It also previews August PCE (headline +0.4%, core +0.3% m/m), noting methodology revisions should cut y/y prints about 0.2pp to 3.6%/3.2% without altering near-term policy. Separately, record net interest costs (3.3% of GDP) echo the 1991 peak, when the 10-year yield was near 7%, implying yields may need to rise further before Washington addresses the deficit; record household balance-sheet ratios (10x assets-to-liabilities) cushion even a 20% equity drawdown. BofA holds an out-of-consensus call for two more 25bp Fed hikes (Oct, Dec) after September's hawkish 25bp move, with 2026 growth trimmed to 2.1% and core PCE seen stuck near 3.3%/2.4% through 2027.
